title: Osstem promotes the KS 3 dental implant ahead of European launch
html:
Osstem Implant

Mon. 23. November 2026

share save

LISBON, Portugal: Osstem Implant is stepping up the promotion of the KS 3 dental implant ahead of its planned European launch in the first quarter of next year. Introduced to clinicians at the European Association for Osseointegration (EAO) congress in Lisbon in September, the implant is designed to provide primary stability in challenging clinical situations, including cases involving soft bone and immediate placement.

The KS 3 builds on Osstem’s existing KS implant system and combines a fully tapered body with deep threads, a dual cutting edge and a sharp apex. The 3° taper is designed to promote gradual bone compression during insertion, while the deep threads provide mechanical engagement with the surrounding bone. The sharp apex facilitates initial entry and helps guide placement. The dual cutting edge combines cutting and non-cutting sections to support controlled insertion while maintaining bone engagement and compression.

The KS 3 is available with different surface treatments, including a sand-blasted and acid-etched surface and a calcium-based surface featuring a resorbable apatite nano-coating. The apatite nano-coating is super-hydrophilic and promotes rapid wetting of the implant surface by blood. This surface treatment is intended to support early bone formation at the implant interface and subsequent osseointegration.

Osstem Implant presented its KS 3 implant at its exhibition booth during the 2026 European Association for Osseointegration congress.

Hands-on sessions highlight KS 3 design

During a presentation introducing the KS 3 at the EAO Innovation Hub, Marta Pinto, marketing manager at Osstem Implant Portugal, discussed the implant’s design features and their contribution to primary stability. She also highlighted the implant’s potential to support immediate loading in suitable clinical circumstances. Congress participants had the opportunity to try out the implant during hands-on sessions at the Osstem exhibition booth, gaining first-hand experience of the implant’s design and intended clinical applications.

Osstem plans to launch the KS 3 commercially in EU markets at the 2027 International Dental Show, which will take place in Cologne in Germany from 16 to 20 March. Further information about the implant, its surface treatments, surgical instrumentation and prosthetic components is available on the Osstem Europe website.
